title: The Day from Which a Vehicle Is Taken to Have Been Off the Road
content:
The days a vehicle protected by the Keyturn Host Protection Plan stands off the road are counted from a day the record settles, and which day that is turns on whether a callout was completed on the roadside cover the vehicle carries in the month before the appraisal.

- Where a callout on the roadside cover the vehicle carries was completed in the month before the appraisal and the vehicle was towed in that month, the days off the road are counted from the day of the most recent completed callout on that cover.
- Where a callout was completed on that cover in that month and the vehicle was not towed in it, they are counted from the day the most recent report was lodged on the register.
- Where no callout was completed on that cover in that month, they are counted from the day the loss is recorded on the most recently opened claim.

### Input, judgement, output

| Callout completed on that cover in the month before the appraisal | Towing recorded in that month | Counted from |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the day of the most recent completed callout on that cover |
| yes | no | the day the most recent report was lodged on the register |
| no | — | the day the loss is recorded on the most recently opened claim |

A callout standing on the cover in any state other than completed is counted for none of the three readings. Where several callouts were completed on that cover in the month, it is the most recent of them that gives the day; and where every completed callout in the month carries no towing distance, the vehicle was not towed.

### What the records show

The callouts and the towing recorded against them are read from the Keyturn Roadside Assistance cover the vehicle carries, over the month before the appraisal and counting only callouts recorded as completed on it. The day the report was lodged is the day of the most recent report on the damage report register for this enrolment, and the day the loss is recorded is the loss day carried on the most recently opened claim.
